phrases.en: Excuse me, where is the check-in counter?
phrases.zh: 不好意思，報到櫃檯在哪裡？
phrases.note: 到機場第一句話。用 'Excuse me' 開頭更有禮貌。

phrases.en: Can I have a window seat, please?
phrases.zh: 可以給我靠窗的座位嗎？
phrases.note: 報到時選位子的必備句型。換成 aisle seat 也可以。

phrases.en: How many bags can I bring?
phrases.note: 確認行李規定。也可以問 carry-on 的限制。

phrases.zh: 我的航班在哪個登機門？
phrases.note: 拿到登機證後可以再確認一次。

phrases.en: What time does the flight leave?
phrases.note: 確認出發時間。也可以用 departure time。

dialogues.title: Checking In at the Counter
dialogues.sit: You arrive at the airport. You go to the check-in counter.
lines: Excuse me, I want to check in.
Sure! Can I see your passport and ticket?
Here is my passport and my ticket.
Thank you. Do you want a window seat or an aisle seat?
OK. How many pieces of luggage do you have?
I have one suitcase and one carry-on.
Please put your suitcase on the scale.
No, it is fine. Here is your boarding pass. Your gate is twelve.
You are welcome. Have a nice flight!
dialogues.tp: Try again: this time ask for an AISLE SEAT and you have TWO suitcases.
dialogues.tn: Student A 重點：確認能正確發出 check in / boarding pass / luggage。每個詞讓學生重複 2-3 次再繼續。注意 th 音 (thank) 和尾音 (seat, flight)。

dialogues.title: Asking for Help at the Airport
dialogues.sit: You cannot find your gate. You ask a worker for help.
lines: Excuse me, can you help me?
Of course! What do you need?
I cannot find my gate. It says gate fifteen.
Gate fifteen is in terminal two. Go straight, then turn left.
OK, thank you for your help!
No problem. Have a safe trip!
dialogues.tp: Try again: your gate is number TWENTY and you also ask where the restroom is.
dialogues.tn: Student A 重點：'Can you help me?' 這句要練到自動反應。注意 fifteen 的 /f/ 發音。

dialogues.title: Checking Your Luggage
dialogues.sit: Your suitcase is too heavy. The staff tells you.
lines: Let me put it on the scale... I am sorry, it is overweight.
It is three kilograms over. You need to pay extra or take some things out.
Can I move some things to my carry-on?
Yes, of course. Take your time.
OK, I moved some things. Can you check again?
It is good now! Here is your boarding pass.
dialogues.tp: Try again: this time you choose to PAY the extra fee instead of moving things.
dialogues.tn: Student A 重點：overweight 是新詞，先教發音再練句子。注意 'take some things out' 的連音。

dialogues.title: Buying Food Before the Flight
dialogues.sit: You are hungry before your flight. You go to a shop in the terminal.
lines: Excuse me, how much is this sandwich?
OK, I will take it. And a water, please.
Sure. That is eleven dollars total.
dialogues.tp: Try again: you want to buy COFFEE and a COOKIE instead.
dialogues.tn: 練習 how much + 數字聽力。Student A 可能對數字反應慢，可多練。

dialogues.title: Finding Your Seat on the Plane
dialogues.sit: You get on the plane and look for your seat.
lines: Excuse me, where is seat fourteen A?
Go down the aisle. It is on the left side.
Thank you! Can I put my carry-on up here?
Yes, in the overhead bin. Let me help you.
You are welcome. Please sit down and fasten your seatbelt.
dialogues.tp: Try again: your seat is TWENTY-TWO B and the overhead bin is full.
dialogues.tn: 練習數字+字母組合 (14A)。Student A 座位號碼要多練幾次。

culture.title: Airport Signs — Reading English Signs
culture.photo: Photo: Airport signs showing Departures, Arrivals, Check-In, Gates, Restrooms, Exit in English.
culture.notes: Airports around the world use English on their signs. Even in non-English countries, you can see words like 'Gate', 'Exit', 'Check-In', and 'Departure'. Learning these words helps you travel anywhere!
qs: Can you read English signs at Taiwan's airports?
Which airport sign word is the most useful to know?
Have you ever been lost at an airport? What happened?

culture.title: How to Line Up — Queuing Culture
culture.photo: Photo: People standing in a neat line at an airport check-in counter. Everyone is patient and waiting their turn.
culture.notes: In many countries, people line up (queue) and wait for their turn. Cutting in line is very rude. At airports, you will see lines for check-in, security, and boarding. Always wait your turn and be patient!
qs: Do people line up in Taiwan? Is it the same as at airports?
What do you do when someone cuts in line?
Do you think airports should have faster lines for some people?

pronunciation.focus: Final Consonants — Say the Whole Word!
pronunciation.fz: 尾音不能省！把整個字說完整
pronunciation.tip: 中文沒有字尾子音，所以中文母語者容易把尾音省掉。seat 不是 see、help 不是 hel。練習時特別注意嘴巴要做出最後一個音！
pronunciation.prac: Practice: 'I need help with my seat and my bag for this flight.'
